findings.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — light-theme value for `.topic-map .links a` was changed from 30% to 70% lightness instead of being preserved, making topic-map link names far lighter and degrading contrast for light-theme users

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — `h3` color light value changed from 20% to 50% lightness instead of preserving 20%/80% pairing, regressing visual weight of topic-map headings on mobile light themes

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:99 — `.custom-message-length` light/dark values inverted (30%/70% instead of 70%/30%), making the character counter hint text visually jarring on both light and dark themes
[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:519 — `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50%, flattening the intended name/title hierarchy so user profile names lose emphasis
[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:494 — same transcription error: `.name` changed from 30% to 50% lightness, erasing the name/title hierarchy on mobile light themes

[ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:89 — embedded-posts pipeline may not import the partial defining `dark-light-choose`, risking a compile error / broken embed CSS for sites using embedded topics; needs verification before merging

[BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — light-theme branch of dark-light-choose received the dark branch's lightness value (70% instead of 30%), inverting light-theme contrast for linked usernames in the small-action block
[BUG] mobile/modal.scss:101 — .custom-message-length light branch dropped from 70% to 30%, inverting both theme branches so desktop and mobile variants of the same rule disagree
[BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 — .name rule light branch changed from 30% to 50%, an unexplained light-theme regression that flattens the typographic hierarchy against .title
[BUG] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — mobile h3 link title light branch changed from 20% to 50% lightness, causing a 30-point contrast loss and disagreeing with its desktop twin

[ADVISORY] mobile/compose.scss:178 — .wmd-input color darken($primary, 40%) left unconverted while surrounding disabled-input rules were converted, making composer input text near-invisible in dark themes
[ADVISORY] No verification of any kind accompanies ~90 changed color rules; a minimal light-branch byte-for-byte preservation check would have caught the four silent light-branch changes

[ADVISORY] The dark-light-choose conversion convention is internally inconsistent (mirrored vs. identical lightness across branches), making future conversions and audits unreliable and collapsing dark-theme contrast hierarchy

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — light-theme link color changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, making reply-notification username links near-white/grey on light backgrounds, a light-theme regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — h3 color changed from 20% to 50% lightness in the light branch, causing mobile small-action headings to lose contrast; not traceable to the dark-theme requirement

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — .custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30%, inverting the intended hint-text-dimmer-than-body hierarchy in light themes; desktop/modal.scss keeps 70%, so mobile and desktop diverge without justification

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 — .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness, washing out the user-profile name in light themes; a light-theme behavior change smuggled into a dark-theme PR

[ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:196 — .icon uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) while adjacent .fa uses 50%; the asymmetry breaks the X%/(100−X)% mirror convention, making notification icons render at a different grey tier and suggesting a transcription error

[ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:33 — color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) left un-migrated on the #wmd-button-adjacent rule while #draft-status is converted, leaving mobile dark-theme composer button text mis-rendered

[ADVISORY] Whole diff — hand-maintained parallel lightness pairs (~90 edits) with several non-mirroring exceptions; a $lightness-mirror SCSS function or dark-light-choose wrapper would mechanically enforce the mirror invariant and prevent recurring transcription errors

[BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — `.name` selector changed the light-theme value from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, inverting light-theme contrast so usernames render in near-background gray instead of dark emphasis text, and reversing the light/dark complement convention (70% light paired with 30% dark).

[BUG] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `.name`-block `h3` changed `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in the light branch, weakening the strongest heading color to mid-gray and causing mobile/desktop title color divergence (desktop kept 20%).

[BUG] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, inverting both branches relative to the identical desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss:94 keeps 70%/30%), so the element renders with opposite weights on mobile vs desktop and light-mode hint text becomes visually shouting.

[BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` light-theme value changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `$lightness: 50%` while adjacent `.title` kept 50% (mobile twin mobile/user.scss:497 has the same unexplained change), collapsing the intentional 30%/50% visual hierarchy and contradicting untouched common/base/user.scss:126.

[ADVISORY] mobile/compose.scss:33 — `.btn-default` directly adjacent to converted lines still has bare `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)` without dark-light-choose treatment while sibling `#draft-status` was converted, leaving the sweep visibly incomplete and signaling a grep-based rather than reviewed conversion.

[BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — `.reply a` color uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` but original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; both branches are inverted relative to the pattern used everywhere else (expected 30%/70%), making light-theme reply usernames washed out and dark-theme ones nearly unreadable.

[BUG] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, with arguments swapped instead of complementary-converted, contradicting desktop/modal.scss:94 which uses 70%/30%; mobile light-theme modal counters become full contrast and dark theme gets the light value.

[BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing light-scheme lightness from 30% to 50% and using 50% instead of the complementary 70% for dark scheme; light-theme user card names lose contrast.

[BUG] mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%/50%, same unexplained lightness rewrite as the desktop file; mobile light-theme user names render at 50% instead of 30%, a visual regression on the light scheme.

[BUG] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `.small-action h3` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, while the identical desktop rule (desktop/topic-post.scss:318) correctly becomes 20%/80%; mobile light-theme small-action titles drop from 20% to 50% contrast.

[ADVISORY] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — the `a` rule inside the names block changed scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) — the light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70%, causing near-invisible username links in light themes; the light branch should preserve the original 30%

[ADVISORY] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — the embedded-content h3 rule became dark-light-choose with 50% lightness in both branches where the original was 30%, making dark-light-choose a no-op with no dark-theme adaptation

[ADVISORY] desktop/user.scss:522 — the .name rule's dark-light-choose uses identical 50%/50% branches where the original light value was 30%; the function is a no-op and the light theme value changed from 30% to 50%
[ADVISORY] mobile/user.scss:496 — .name changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), an identical-branch no-op pattern with no dark-theme differentiation

[ADVISORY] mobile/modal.scss:102 — .custom-message-length became dark-light-choose(30%, 70%) while desktop/modal.scss:94 uses (70%, 30%); the mobile light-theme value was inverted relative to both the original code and the desktop version of the same rule

[ADVISORY] Mechanical ~40-file rewrite with no automated verification: a scripted check or lint asserting the light branch matches the pre-change value and that the two branches differ would have caught all the no-op and inverted dark-light-choose conversions, but nothing in the pipeline performs that role

At least one dark-light-choose replacement changes the light-theme value as well: desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, and desktop/user.scss:522 use a different $lightness in the new first argument than the old rule

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — `.names a` rule changed light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, dropping bold username links to pale gray on light themes and losing visual distinction and contrast

[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` first argument changed from 70% to 30%, inverting the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:94) and causing mobile/desktop light-theme divergence in the custom message length hint

[ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` changed from 30% to 50% lightness, either contradicting the PR's stated "dark theme only" purpose or smuggling an unflagged visual change reducing user-card/profile name contrast on light themes

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — light-theme value for `.topic-map .links a` was changed from 30% to 70% lightness instead of being preserved, making topic-map link names far lighter and degrading contrast for light-theme users

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` around the reported line (~288), the diff shows `a { font-weight: bold; ... }` changing from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. Since `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` uses the first value for the light theme, this effectively changes the light-theme lightness from 30% to 70%, making the link color much lighter in light mode (and darker in dark mode) compared to the previous behavior. That matches the finding’s claim about degraded light-theme contrast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:179 — `h3` color light value changed from 20% to 50% lightness instead of preserving 20%/80% pairing, regressing visual weight of topic-map headings on mobile light themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` at the `a.star h3` rule (around line ~179), the color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This is a real, diff-verifiable change in light-theme lightness (20% → 50%) and it is inconsistent with many other replacements in the diff that preserve the original lightness value for the light-theme branch and use a complementary value for the dark-theme branch (e.g., 20%/80%). That inconsistency can reasonably be treated as an introduced UI defect (reduced visual contrast/weight on mobile light theme).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:99 — `.custom-message-length` light/dark values inverted (30%/70% instead of 70%/30%), making the character counter hint text visually jarring on both light and dark themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` the `.custom-message-length` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This is inconsistent with the same selector in `desktop/modal.scss`, which uses `dark-light-choose(...70%, ...30%)`, and with the general pattern elsewhere in the diff (light theme uses lighter `$primary` values while dark theme uses darker `$secondary` values). The mobile values appear inverted (30/70), likely producing wrong contrast in both themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:519 — `.name` light value changed from 30% to 50%, flattening the intended name/title hierarchy so user profile names lose emphasis
[BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss:494 — same transcription error: `.name` changed from 30% to 50% lightness, erasing the name/title hierarchy on mobile light themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss` the `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, while `.title` remains at 50% lightness. On the light-theme branch (first arg to `dark-light-choose`), this makes `.name` and `.title` the same lightness, removing the previous visual hierarchy that existed when `.name` was 30%. This regression is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss:89 — embedded-posts pipeline may not import the partial defining `dark-light-choose`, risking a compile error / broken embed CSS for sites using embedded topics; needs verification before merging

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` to use `dark-light-choose(...)` (e.g., `a.new-user { color: dark-light-choose(...) }`). Whether the embed/"embedded-posts" stylesheet compilation context imports/defines `dark-light-choose` is not shown in this diff, so a compile break cannot be verified here. However, the concern is specific and diff-grounded: introducing a new Sass function dependency in `embed.css.scss` could require ensuring the embed pipeline includes its definition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — light-theme branch of dark-light-choose received the dark branch's lightness value (70% instead of 30%), inverting light-theme contrast for linked usernames in the small-action block
[BUG] mobile/modal.scss:101 — .custom-message-length light branch dropped from 70% to 30%, inverting both theme branches so desktop and mobile variants of the same rule disagree

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which does drop the `$primary` (first) branch from 70% to 30%. This is inconsistent with the corresponding rule in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/modal.scss`, which is updated to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. Given the widespread pattern in the diff using higher lightness for the `$primary` branch and lower for the `$secondary` branch, the mobile change appears inverted/mistyped and would cause desktop vs mobile to render different colors for the same UI element under the same theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 — .name rule light branch changed from 30% to 50%, an unexplained light-theme regression that flattens the typographic hierarchy against .title

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show the specific change the finding cites: in `desktop/user.scss` and `mobile/user.scss`, `.name` changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, i.e., the light-branch value becomes 50%. In the same blocks, `.title` is also set to 50%, so the prior visual hierarchy (name darker than title) is removed. However, this is a stylistic/visual regression concern rather than a clearly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — mobile h3 link title light branch changed from 20% to 50% lightness, causing a 30-point contrast loss and disagreeing with its desktop twin

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` the `a.star h3` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, i.e. the light-theme branch goes from 20% to 50% lightness. In the corresponding desktop rule (`app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`), `h3` remains `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), ...)`, so mobile now diverges from desktop and becomes notably lighter in light mode, matching the finding’s claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] mobile/compose.scss:178 — .wmd-input color darken($primary, 40%) left unconverted while surrounding disabled-input rules were converted, making composer input text near-invisible in dark themes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss`, the disabled-state backgrounds for `#reply-title:disabled` and `.wmd-input:disabled` were converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`, but the enabled `.wmd-input` text color remains `color: darken($primary, 40%);`. Given this PR’s broad conversion from `scale-color($primary, ...)` to `dark-light-choose(...)` for dark-theme readability, leaving a hardcoded `darken($primary, 40%)` here is a diff-grounded inconsistency that can plausibly make composer input text too dark in dark themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No verification of any kind accompanies ~90 changed color rules; a minimal light-branch byte-for-byte preservation check would have caught the four silent light-branch changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows many SCSS color rules changing from `scale-color($primary, ...)` to `dark-light-choose(...)`, but the finding’s claims about (1) “no verification accompanies” these changes and (2) a specific “four silent light-branch changes” are not verifiable from the diff alone (there are no tests/verification artifacts shown, and the semantics of which argument `dark-light-choose` uses for the “light branch” are not present here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dark-light-choose conversion convention is internally inconsistent (mirrored vs. identical lightness across branches), making future conversions and audits unreliable and collapsing dark-theme contrast hierarchy

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows no single, consistent mapping rule for converting `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X)` into `dark-light-choose(...)`: many replacements use identical lightness on both branches (e.g. `...50%` → `primary 50% / secondary 50%` across multiple files), others use mirrored complements (e.g. `primary 70% / secondary 30%`, `primary 35% / secondary 65%`, `primary 40% / secondary 60%`), and at least one looks particularly inconsistent with the original intent (in `desktop/topic-post.scss` around the “a { font-weight: bold; }” block, original `lightness: 30%` becomes `dark-light-choose(primary 70%, secondary 30%)`, changing the light-theme value from 30% to 70%). Also `mobile/modal.scss` sets `.custom-message-length` to `primary 30% / secondary 70%` whereas `desktop/modal.scss` uses `primary 70% / secondary 30%` for the same selector name, suggesting ad-hoc choices. This supports the finding’s maintainability/audit concern, though the claimed contrast collapse is not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — light-theme link color changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, making reply-notification username links near-white/grey on light backgrounds, a light-theme regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix

This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag the same change: in the light theme, `.topic-meta-data h5 a` link color was adjusted from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `70%`, which likely reduces contrast and harms readability (appearing near-white/grey on light backgrounds).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — h3 color changed from 20% to 50% lightness in the light branch, causing mobile small-action headings to lose contrast; not traceable to the dark-theme requirement

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` the `a.star h3` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This is not just wrapping the existing light-theme value with `dark-light-choose`; it also changes the light-branch lightness from 20% to 50%, which is a concrete behavioral change in the light theme and can plausibly reduce contrast for that heading compared to before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — .custom-message-length light value changed from 70% to 30%, inverting the intended hint-text-dimmer-than-body hierarchy in light themes; desktop/modal.scss keeps 70%, so mobile and desktop diverge without justification

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which (by function name/argument order) likely makes the light-theme hint text much darker (30%) than before. In contrast, `desktop/modal.scss` sets the light-theme value to 70% via `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, so mobile and desktop now diverge and the mobile light-theme hierarchy is plausibly inverted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 and mobile/user.scss:497 — .name light-theme color changed from 30% to 50% lightness, washing out the user-profile name in light themes; a light-theme behavior change smuggled into a dark-theme PR

[ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss:196 — .icon uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%) while adjacent .fa uses 50%; the asymmetry breaks the X%/(100−X)% mirror convention, making notification icons render at a different grey tier and suggesting a transcription error

adjudication.rationale: In `common/base/header.scss` the diff changes notifications dropdown colors to `dark-light-choose(...)`: `.fa` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 50%), scale-color($secondary, 50%))` and `.icon` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`. The claimed “mirror convention” is actually satisfied within each `dark-light-choose` pair (30/70 and 50/50). The finding incorrectly treats the difference between `.fa` and `.icon` as a convention violation; the diff does not show this as a definite bug or transcription error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss:33 — color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%) left un-migrated on the #wmd-button-adjacent rule while #draft-status is converted, leaving mobile dark-theme composer button text mis-rendered

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss, the rule near the shown hunk keeps `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%);` unchanged while the adjacent `#draft-status` color is migrated to `dark-light-choose(...)`. The diff therefore does leave a likely-unmigrated color value in that area, but the claim that it definitively causes "mobile dark-theme composer button text mis-rendered" is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Whole diff — hand-maintained parallel lightness pairs (~90 edits) with several non-mirroring exceptions; a $lightness-mirror SCSS function or dark-light-choose wrapper would mechanically enforce the mirror invariant and prevent recurring transcription errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many single `scale-color($primary, $lightness: X)` uses with `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: Y))`, where Y is often the “mirror” (e.g., 70/30, 60/40, 40/60, 35/65, 25/75, 75/25) or equal (50/50). This creates a large amount of hand-maintained paired values across many files, and the diff shows at least a few non-mirroring/inconsistent pairs that look like potential transcription drift (e.g., `desktop/topic-post.scss` changes a link from primary lightness 30 to a `dark-light-choose(... $primary 70%, $secondary 30%)`, and `mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` to `$primary 30% / $secondary 70%` while the analogous desktop rule uses 70/30). A helper (mirror function/wrapper) would reduce duplication and mechanically enforce the intended invariant, making the change less error-prone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — `.name` selector changed the light-theme value from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, inverting light-theme contrast so usernames render in near-background gray instead of dark emphasis text, and reversing the light/dark complement convention (70% light paired with 30% dark).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` around the hunk starting at `@@ -288`, the link color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This is a concrete inversion of the light-theme value (30% -> 70%), and it’s inconsistent with the dominant pattern elsewhere in the diff where light theme typically uses a darker primary (e.g., 30–40%) and dark theme uses a lighter secondary (e.g., 60–70%). While the finding misnames the selector as `.name` (the diff shows an `a { ... }` rule in that region), the underlying issue—swapped light/dark lightness choices likely reducing light-theme contrast—is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `.name`-block `h3` changed `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` in the light branch, weakening the strongest heading color to mid-gray and causing mobile/desktop title color divergence (desktop kept 20%).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` at the `a.star h3` rule (around the `@@ -179,7 +179,7 @@` hunk), the light-theme value changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, which materially alters the light-branch color from 20% to 50%. In the same PR, the corresponding desktop rule keeps 20% in the light branch (`desktop/topic-post.scss` h3 uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), ...)`). This creates a verifiable mobile/desktop divergence and likely an unintended visual regression in light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, inverting both branches relative to the identical desktop rule (desktop/modal.scss:94 keeps 70%/30%), so the element renders with opposite weights on mobile vs desktop and light-mode hint text becomes visually shouting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` while `desktop/modal.scss` sets the same selector to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This is a clear inversion of the two branches between mobile and desktop, creating inconsistent theming behavior across platforms and likely wrong light/dark emphasis for this hint text.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` light-theme value changed from `$lightness: 30%` to `$lightness: 50%` while adjacent `.title` kept 50% (mobile twin mobile/user.scss:497 has the same unexplained change), collapsing the intentional 30%/50% visual hierarchy and contradicting untouched common/base/user.scss:126.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `.name` in `desktop/user.scss` and `mobile/user.scss` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, while adjacent `.title` stays at 50%. Meanwhile `common/base/user.scss` keeps `.name` at 30% (now via `dark-light-choose(...30%..., ...70%...)`). This creates an inconsistency and likely alters the intended visual hierarchy, but from the diff alone it's not provably a functional defect vs. an intentional design adjustment for theming/contrast.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/compose.scss` around the shown hunk, a line immediately preceding the converted `#draft-status` still reads `color: scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%);` while `#draft-status` was changed to `dark-light-choose(...)`. The finding’s specific mention of `.btn-default` isn’t directly verifiable from the provided diff context, but the underlying point—that adjacent theming-related `scale-color(...)` usage remains unconverted and may indicate an incomplete dark/light sweep—is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/topic-post.scss:288 — `.reply a` color uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` but original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; both branches are inverted relative to the pattern used everywhere else (expected 30%/70%), making light-theme reply usernames washed out and dark-theme ones nearly unreadable.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` the `.reply ... a` rule changes from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));`. This is inverted compared to the consistent pattern elsewhere in the same diff (e.g. multiple rules use `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, 30%), scale-color($secondary, 70%))`), so it likely makes the light theme too light (70%) and the dark theme too dark (30%) for reply usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))` from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, with arguments swapped instead of complementary-converted, contradicting desktop/modal.scss:94 which uses 70%/30%; mobile light-theme modal counters become full contrast and dark theme gets the light value.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, while the corresponding `desktop/modal.scss` uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing light-scheme lightness from 30% to 50% and using 50% instead of the complementary 70% for dark scheme; light-theme user card names lose contrast.
matched_golden_ids: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core regression noted in the golden comment: in desktop/user styles, the `.name` color changes the light-theme `$primary` lightness from 30% to 50% (while other changes generally keep the original light-theme value and use `$secondary` for dark). The candidate is more specific and adds an extra critique about the dark-scheme percentage, but it still identifies the same underlying issue (unexpected 30%→50% change for light).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to 50%/50%, same unexplained lightness rewrite as the desktop file; mobile light-theme user names render at 50% instead of 30%, a visual regression on the light scheme.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows in `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` the `a.star h3` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (hunk around `@@ -179`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — the `a` rule inside the names block changed scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) — the light-theme value was silently changed from 30% to 70%, causing near-invisible username links in light themes; the light branch should preserve the original 30%
matched_golden_ids: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Candidate flags the same selector change: color was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(...$primary 70%..., ...$secondary 30%), highlighting that the light-theme branch shifted from 30% to 70% lightness and should preserve 30%. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — the embedded-content h3 rule became dark-light-choose with 50% lightness in both branches where the original was 30%, making dark-light-choose a no-op with no dark-theme adaptation

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, the shown `h3` change is within the `a.star { h3 { ... } }` block, not an `embedded-content h3` rule. Also, the original value was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, not 30%. Finally, `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary,...), scale-color($secondary,...))` is not a no-op even if both use `50%` lightness, because `$primary` and `$secondary` are different variables, so it still adapts between themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] desktop/user.scss:522 — the .name rule's dark-light-choose uses identical 50%/50% branches where the original light value was 30%; the function is a no-op and the light theme value changed from 30% to 50%

adjudication.rationale: In desktop/user.scss the .name rule changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. While the light-theme lightness does change from 30% to 50%, the finding's core claim that the `dark-light-choose` is a “no-op” due to “identical branches” is not supported by the diff: the two branches are not identical expressions (`$primary` vs `$secondary`), so the function can still select different colors by theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] mobile/user.scss:496 — .name changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to dark-light-choose(50%, 50%), an identical-branch no-op pattern with no dark-theme differentiation

adjudication.rationale: In mobile/user.scss the `.name` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The two branches are not identical (primary vs secondary), and it is not a no-op; it both changes the lightness (30% -> 50% for the light branch) and introduces a different value for the dark branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] mobile/modal.scss:102 — .custom-message-length became dark-light-choose(30%, 70%) while desktop/modal.scss:94 uses (70%, 30%); the mobile light-theme value was inverted relative to both the original code and the desktop version of the same rule

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss`, `.custom-message-length` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which makes the light-theme color much darker (30% vs the prior 70%) and also reverses the usual dark/light pairing compared to `desktop/modal.scss` (which uses `dark-light-choose(...70%, ...30%)`) and most other edits in the diff. This inconsistency is verifiable in the diff and likely an accidental inversion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Mechanical ~40-file rewrite with no automated verification: a scripted check or lint asserting the light branch matches the pre-change value and that the two branches differ would have caught all the no-op and inverted dark-light-choose conversions, but nothing in the pipeline performs that role

adjudication.rationale: The diff is a large mechanical rewrite replacing many `scale-color($primary, ...)` usages with `dark-light-choose(...)` across numerous SCSS files. Within the diff, there are examples where the “light” branch no longer matches the pre-change value (suggesting the kind of inversion/no-op risk the finding describes), e.g. in `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` an `a { color: ... }` changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, and `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` changes `custom-message-length` from primary 70% to primary 30%. A scripted assertion that the first argument preserves the old value would have detected such mismatches. However, the claim about “nothing in the pipeline performs that role” is not verifiable from the diff alone, so this is best treated as a diff-grounded process/testing concern rather than a directly proven CI failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: At least one dark-light-choose replacement changes the light-theme value as well: desktop/topic-post.scss:291, mobile/modal.scss:102, and desktop/user.scss:522 use a different $lightness in the new first argument than the old rule
matched_golden_ids: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The golden issue is that the replacement changes the light-theme $lightness value (70% to 30%) in topic-post, making text darker. The candidate flags that the dark-light-choose replacement alters the light-theme $lightness compared to the old rule and explicitly includes desktop/topic-post.scss, which is the same underlying problem (light theme lightness changed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — `.names a` rule changed light-theme value from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 70%, dropping bold username links to pale gray on light themes and losing visual distinction and contrast

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` near line ~288, the `.names a` rule keeps `font-weight: bold` but changes the light-theme color from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`. Since `dark-light-choose` uses the first argument for light theme, this is a concrete change from 30% to 70% lightness in light mode, which would make the link color significantly lighter and plausibly reduce contrast/visual distinction as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` first argument changed from 70% to 30%, inverting the desktop counterpart (desktop/modal.scss:94) and causing mobile/desktop light-theme divergence in the custom message length hint

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `desktop/modal.scss` sets `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, preserving the prior light-theme value (70% lightness on `$primary`). But `mobile/modal.scss` changes `.custom-message-length` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, which swaps/inverts the light vs dark arguments compared to desktop and also changes the light-theme value from the previous 70% to 30%. This is inconsistent with the surrounding pattern in the diff (typically keeping the first argument equal to the old `scale-color($primary, ...)`) and would cause mobile/desktop divergence in the light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` changed from 30% to 50% lightness, either contradicting the PR's stated "dark theme only" purpose or smuggling an unflagged visual change reducing user-card/profile name contrast on light themes

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss, the `.name` rule does change its light-theme color value: it was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. That means the first (light) branch uses 50% lightness instead of the previous 30%, which is a real, diff-grounded visual change on light themes and is inconsistent with the otherwise mostly 1:1 replacements to `dark-light-choose(...)` seen elsewhere in the diff. This is a legitimate review concern about unintended scope/contrast changes, but it’s not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — `h3` changed from 20% to 50% lightness while desktop/topic-post.scss keeps 20% for the same selector, causing mobile/desktop light-theme contrast divergence outside the PR's stated scope

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss` changes `a.star h3` from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, which makes the light-theme (primary) value 50% instead of 20%. In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss`, the corresponding `a.star h3` remains at 20% (now wrapped in `dark-light-choose(...20%..., ...80%...)`). This mobile/desktop divergence for the same selector is directly verifiable from the diff; whether it's intended is unclear, but it's a concrete, reviewable consistency/scope concern rather than a clearly broken behavior.
